question.rationale: No supported boundary is declared for the selected models, so use discrimination rather than a boundary probe. Existing prediction failures show that similar one-reversal schedules can produce large late-trajectory errors, while other trajectories remain well predicted; the current records do not establish a single descriptive-feature boundary. Varying reversal depth directly changes the opposite-pulse magnitude while holding the initial pulse schedule fixed, probing how the models' different latent-memory structures respond. The amplitude range stays within the allowed input limit, and the selected models have distinct fitted structures and held-out behavior (including the marked contrast between b4_r1's poor high-jump predictions and b4_r2's lower grouped-CV NMSE).
question.claim: Across the tested conditioning amplitudes and both signs, reversal-depth variation will yield at least one pair of value levels whose predicted output trajectories differ by the discrimination threshold for at least two selected models; this is a local model-discrimination claim, not a universal law.
question.update_if_violated: If the compiler finds insufficient separation, or observed paired trajectories fail to distinguish the selected models beyond measurement noise, retain no boundary claim and revise the candidate structures or choose a different one-factor family; do not interpret that result as proof that reversal depth is irrelevant.
